```text
1	# marvin boot binaries — what they are and how to (re)build them
2	
3	at91bootstrap is marvin's first-stage boot: RomBOOT loads it, it brings up the
4	266 MHz clocks + the in-package DDR3L (Winbond `W632GU6NB12I`), then either hands
5	off to the application or — for the JTAG dev loop — stops and waits.
6	
7	All bootstraps here are built from at91bootstrap **v4.0.13** source (recipes
8	below), so their provenance is known.
9	
10	| File | Medium / use | Built from defconfig |
11	|------|--------------|----------------------|
12	| `sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf` | **JTAG load-to-RAM** (init-and-stop). Used by `../openocd/load-ram.sh`. | `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone` |
13	| `sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin` | **NAND** boot (SAM-BA `writeboot`) | `sam9x75_curiosity_pronf_uboot` |
14	| `sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13-pmecchead.bin` | **NAND** boot via the macOS u-boot/JTAG path (`../openocd/program-nand.sh`) | as above + PMECC header prepended (`make-pmecchead.sh`) |
15	| `sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin` | **NAND flasher**, RAM-loaded over JTAG by `../openocd/program-nand.sh` (drives `nand erase`/`nand write`; not itself flashed to the board) | u-boot `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash` (recipe below) |
16	| `sam9x7-dataflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin` | **QSPI** boot (SAM-BA `writeboot`) | `sam9x75_curiosity_prodf_qspi_uboot` |
17	| `sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin` | **microSD** boot (copied to FAT as `boot.bin`) | `sam9x75_curiosity_prosd_uboot` + `IMAGE_NAME=harmony.bin` |
18	| `make-pmecchead.sh` | Prepend the SAM9X7 ROM PMECC header to a NAND bootstrap (so a plain `nand write` is RomBOOT-bootable; SAM-BA's `writeboot` does this itself) | — |
19	| `nand_flash.bat`, `qspi_flash.bat` | SAM-BA flashing scripts (Linux/Windows host) | — |
20	
21	The media bootstraps all jump to **`0x23F00000`** (`CONFIG_JUMP_ADDR`) — exactly
22	where marvin links and runs — so marvin (`out/harmony.bin`) is the second stage.
23	
24	## Boot order (SAM9X75 ROM)
25	
26	The ROM tries NVM in a fixed sequential fall-through (first valid image wins);
27	order is customizable only via the OTP Boot Configuration Packet:
28	
29	> **SD/eMMC (SDMMC0) → SD/eMMC (SDMMC1) → QSPI → NAND (SMC) → SPI (FLEXCOM5)**
30	
31	So **SD outranks NAND, and QSPI sits between them.** Useful consequences:
32	- NAND = resident firmware; **SD = override/recovery** (a valid card boots first,
33	  no jumper change; remove it to fall back to NAND).
34	- For NAND to boot, **QSPI must hold no valid image** (erase it or keep JP4/QSPI-CS
35	  out) — otherwise QSPI boots before NAND.
36	- For the JTAG dev loop we pull JP3 (NAND) + JP4 (QSPI) and use no card, so the
37	  ROM falls all the way through to the SAM-BA monitor.
38	
39	## Board ↔ defconfig
40	
41	The **SAM9X75 Curiosity Hybrid (cHybrid)** maps to the at91bootstrap
42	**`sam9x75_curiosity_pro_*`** defconfigs (confirmed by the on-board red LED on
43	PIOC 14 — `curiosity_pro` uses PC14, plain `curiosity` uses PC19; DDR is identical
44	across both). All variants here use the in-package `W632GU6NB12I` DDR3L.
45	
46	## Prerequisites
47	
48	- **at91bootstrap source** (this was built from `v4.0.13`):
49	  ```sh
50	  git clone https://github.com/linux4sam/at91bootstrap
51	  # in-use clone for this project: ~/Projects/microchip/at91bootstrap
52	  ```
53	- **ARM bare-metal toolchain** — Arm GNU Toolchain (this build used 15.2.Rel1).
54	  It is installed but not on `PATH`; add its `bin` dir:
55	  ```sh
56	  export PATH="/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH"
57	  ```
58	  (Any `arm-none-eabi-` cross-gcc works; XC32 is *not* used for at91bootstrap.)
59	
60	## Build the JTAG load-to-RAM bootstrap (`sam9x7-boot-none-*.elf`)
61	
62	This is the `bkptnone` defconfig — `CONFIG_INIT_AND_STOP=y`: it inits clocks + DDR
63	and then **loops**, leaving MMU/caches off, so a debugger can load a binary into
64	the freshly-initialized DDR. (It does *not* issue a `bkpt`, so it is harmless with
65	no debugger attached.)
66	
67	```sh
68	cd ~/Projects/microchip/at91bootstrap
69	export PATH="/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH"
70	
71	make mrproper
72	make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone_defconfig
73	make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
74	```
75	
76	Output lands in `build/binaries/`:
77	
78	```
79	build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf   <- copy this here
80	build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.bin   (raw image; not needed for JTAG load)
81	build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.map
82	```
83	
84	Copy the ELF into this folder (the `.elf` is what `load_image` consumes; it
85	carries the entry point, `0x300000`):
86	
87	```sh
88	cp build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf \
89	   <repo>/firmware/marvin/binaries/
90	```
91	
92	If the version string in the filename changes (newer at91bootstrap), update the
93	`BOOTSTRAP_ELF` default in `../openocd/load-ram.sh` to match.
94	
95	The `..._bkptnone_defconfig` contents (for reference):
96	
97	```
98	CONFIG_INIT_AND_STOP=y
99	CONFIG_SAM9X7=y
100	CONFIG_DDR_SET_BY_DEVICE=y
101	CONFIG_DDR_W632GU6NB12I=y
102	CONFIG_BOARD_QUIRK_SAM9X75_CURIOSITY=y
103	CONFIG_LED_*    # red on PC14 (curiosity_pro)
104	```
105	
106	## Build the production (standalone-boot) bootstraps
107	
108	These configs are named `*_uboot_*` by convention but are **not** u-boot-specific
109	— they load the next-stage binary from flash into DRAM (`0x23F00000`) and jump.
110	No actual u-boot / Linux is involved; marvin (`harmony.bin`) is the second stage.
111	
112	- **NAND / QSPI** load the app from a **raw flash offset** (`CONFIG_IMG_ADDRESS`,
113	  `0x40000`) — the filename is irrelevant on-device, so these keep their stock
114	  `-uboot-` build-name suffix.
115	- **SD** loads the app from **FAT by filename** (`CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME`). The stock
116	  default is `u-boot.bin`; we override it to **`harmony.bin`** (the Harmony MPU
117	  convention, and consistent with the NAND/QSPI host files). at91bootstrap then
118	  auto-names the output `...-sdcardboot-harmony-...`.
119	
120	```sh
121	cd ~/Projects/microchip/at91bootstrap
122	export PATH="/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH"
123	
124	# NAND  (raw offset; filename unused)
125	make mrproper && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pronf_uboot_defconfig     && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
126	# QSPI  (raw offset; filename unused)
127	make mrproper && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_prodf_qspi_uboot_defconfig && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
128	# microSD — override the FAT second-stage filename to harmony.bin
129	make mrproper && make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_prosd_uboot_defconfig
130	sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME=.*|CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME="harmony.bin"|' .config   # macOS sed
131	make CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi-
132	# artifacts: build/binaries/sam9x7-{nandflashboot,dataflashboot}-uboot-4.0.13.bin
133	#            build/binaries/sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin
134	# (mrproper wipes build/, so copy each .bin out before the next build.)
135	```
136	
137	### Flashing
138	
139	- **NAND (macOS, no SAM-BA)** — `../openocd/program-nand.sh` RAM-loads the u-boot
140	  flasher over JTAG and `nand write`s the boot region + marvin. The boot region
141	  uses the PMECC-headed bootstrap (`*-pmecchead.bin`); see
142	  `../openocd/program-nand.md`. **Validated** booting marvin standalone from NAND.
143	- **NAND / QSPI (Linux/Windows)** — SAM-BA. See `nand_flash.bat` / `qspi_flash.bat`:
144	  bootstrap via `writeboot`, marvin via `write harmony.bin:0x40000`. (SAM-BA's
145	  `nandflash` applet writes the PMECC/boot header the ROM expects — the same header
146	  `make-pmecchead.sh` prepends for the macOS path.)
147	- **microSD** — `../openocd/make-sdcard.sh` on macOS. It writes the SD bootstrap as
148	  `boot.bin` (what the ROM looks for) and marvin as **`harmony.bin`** (the SD
149	  bootstrap's `CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME`).
150	
151	> **QSPI over JTAG from macOS** is still open R&D — OpenOCD has no SAM9X7 QSPI
152	> driver and the u-boot QSPI-boot flasher path isn't wired up here (u-boot's `sf`
153	> could drive it; check whether QSPI boot needs an analogous header). BOSSA is
154	> **not** applicable (it programs Cortex-M on-chip flash over the SAM-BA protocol,
155	> not SAM9 external NVM, and not over JTAG).
156	
157	## Build the NAND flasher u-boot (`sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-*.bin`)
158	
159	This is **not** a boot stage — it's u-boot RAM-loaded over JTAG to drive NAND (see
160	`../openocd/program-nand.md`). Source: the linux4microchip u-boot fork,
161	<https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp> (branch `linux4microchip-2026.04`,
162	v2025.07 base), built with `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig`. Any
163	`arm-none-eabi-` cross toolchain works. macOS specifics: use Homebrew `gmake`
164	(stock make 3.81 can't parse u-boot's Makefile) and pass OpenSSL via the
165	**environment** (command-line `HOST_EXTRACFLAGS` clobbers the bundled-dtc include
166	path); adjust the OpenSSL prefix for your host.
167	
168	```sh
169	git clone -b linux4microchip-2026.04 https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp.git
170	cd u-boot-mchp
171	# ensure an arm-none-eabi- cross-gcc is on PATH (e.g. the Arm GNU Toolchain)
172	export HOST_EXTRACFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"   # macOS host-tool deps
173	export HOSTLDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"
174	gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig
175	gmake CROSS_COMPILE=arm-none-eabi- -j8
176	cp u-boot.bin <repo>/firmware/marvin/binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin
177	```
178
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:08:03Z)**_

Yes — and the mechanism already exists in the tree you're building from. No source edits needed.

## How it works

at91bootstrap has a generic "drive a PIO pin to a fixed level at boot" facility dressed up as the **on-board LED** config. [`driver/led.c`](driver/led.c) just calls `pio_set_gpio_output(pin, value)` for up to three Kconfig-defined channels (R/G/B), and `hw_init()` calls `at91_leds_init()` very early — *before* clocks/DDR, and unconditionally on the INIT_AND_STOP (bkptnone) path too. So it runs in your JTAG load-to-RAM bootstrap.

For the non-PIO4 SAM9X7 PIO, `pio_set_gpio_output(pin, 0)` ([at91_pio.c:340](../../../at91bootstrap/driver/at91_pio.c#L340)) does exactly what you want: disable IRQ, **disable pull-up**, `CODR` (drive low), `OER` (output enable), `PER` (GPIO mode). That's a clean push-pull output driven low.

## The catch

There are only **3 channels** (R/G/B), and your `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone` defconfig already uses all three for the RGB LED: R=PC14, G=PC21, B=PC20. So Kconfig-only works **if you can spare one channel**. E.g. repurpose blue to PC18:

```
CONFIG_LED_B_ON_PIOC=y
CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=18
CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=0
```

`VALUE=0` is literally the level written, so PC18 comes up as output-low. The trade-off is you lose the blue LED (PC20) on that build.

If you need PC18 low **and** want to keep all three RGB LEDs, Kconfig alone can't — you'd add one `pio_set_gpio_output(AT91C_PIN_PC(18), 0);` line (the natural spot is the board quirk hook in [board_hw_init.c](../../../at91bootstrap/driver/board_hw_init.c), which already does this kind of pin poke). But that's a source change, which is what you were trying to avoid.

Want me to wire up a `marvin`-specific defconfig (or a small build recipe note in the binaries README) for the PC18-low variant?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:12:30Z)**_

Traced it fully. Here's the complete LED story in at91bootstrap — it's much simpler than the dynamics suggest.

## at91bootstrap touches the LEDs exactly once

The *only* LED code is `at91_leds_init()`, called from `hw_init()` at [sam9x7.c:291](../../../at91bootstrap/device/sam9x7/sam9x7.c#L291) — right at the start, before clocks/DDR. It does three one-shot writes and never touches the pins again:

```c
pio_set_gpio_output(R, CONFIG_LED_R_VALUE);   // PC14 ← 0
pio_set_gpio_output(G, CONFIG_LED_G_VALUE);   // PC21 ← 1
pio_set_gpio_output(B, CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE);   // PC20 ← 0
```

Your defconfigs set only the **pins**, so the values fall through to the Kconfig defaults ([Kconfig:514-592](../../../at91bootstrap/Kconfig#L514)): **R=0, G=1, B=0**. There is no blink loop, no error/status path, no later toggle anywhere in the tree — I grepped every `.c`/`.h`; `at91_leds_init` is the sole consumer.

## So what you're actually seeing

- **RED at RomBOOT** — pre-at91bootstrap. Either the ROM or just the power-on/reset state of PC14. Not at91bootstrap.
- **RED off → GREEN on** — that's the *single* `at91_leds_init()` write flipping the pins to (R=0, G=1, B=0). It happens the instant at91bootstrap begins `hw_init()`, **not** when it loads the next stage. The red→green isn't a sequence; it's one static assignment that happens to differ from the pre-boot state.
- **All off** — your app (marvin) reclaims the pins.

This also tells you the board's RGB LED is wired **active-high** (pin high = lit): R=0/G=1/B=0 producing "red off, green on, blue off" only makes sense that way.

## Blue: no predefined use

No. Blue (PC20) is configured purely so `at91_leds_init()` can drive it to its initial value **0 = off**, and it's never referenced again. None of R/G/B carry any runtime/status meaning in at91bootstrap — blue is just initialized off and left alone.

Practical upshot for your earlier PC18 question: the **blue channel is the natural one to repurpose** — it conveys nothing, and you'd only be giving up an LED that at91bootstrap deliberately holds off anyway.

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Prepend the SAM9X7 ROM-code NAND boot header to an at91bootstrap binary, so the
3	# boot region can be written by a plain `nand write` (the u-boot/JTAG path in
4	# ../openocd/program-nand.md) instead of SAM-BA's `writeboot` (which synthesizes
5	# the header itself).
6	#
7	# The ROM reads page 0 without ECC, expecting 52 copies of a 32-bit word encoding
8	# the NAND/PMECC params, with the bootstrap code at offset 0xD0 (SAM9X7 Data Sheet
9	# DS60001813D, "NAND Flash Specific Header Detection"). The word MUST match the
10	# actual chip (u-boot `nand info`), NOT at91bootstrap addpmecchead.py's SAM9X7
11	# defaults (2048/64/4) — this board's NAND is 4096/256/8-bit/512 -> 0xc2605007.
12	#
13	# The header word + offset math is inlined here (mirrors at91bootstrap
14	# scripts/pmecc_head.py) so this is self-contained — no external tree needed.
15	#
16	# Usage: ./make-pmecchead.sh [in.bin] [out.bin] [page oob eccbits sector]
17	set -euo pipefail
18	here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
19	IN="${1:-$here/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin}"
20	OUT="${2:-$here/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13-pmecchead.bin}"
21	PAGE="${3:-4096}"; OOB="${4:-256}"; ECC="${5:-8}"; SECTOR="${6:-512}"
22	
23	python3 - "$IN" "$OUT" "$PAGE" "$OOB" "$ECC" "$SECTOR" <<'PY'
24	import sys, struct
25	inp, out, page, oob, ecc, sector = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], *map(int, sys.argv[3:7])
26	
27	# ecc bytes per sector for BCH: m = 12 + sector/512 (Galois field degree)
28	ecc_bytes = ((12 + sector // 512) * ecc + 7) // 8
29	nb_sectors = page // sector
30	ecc_offset = oob - nb_sectors * ecc_bytes
31	
32	# bitfield codes (pmecc_head.json): index into the "meaning" maps
33	sectors_code = {1: 0, 2: 1, 4: 2, 8: 3}[nb_sectors]
34	ecc_code     = {2: 0, 4: 1, 8: 2, 12: 3, 24: 4}[ecc]
35	sector_code  = {512: 0, 1024: 1}[sector]
36	
37	word = (
38	    (1            << 0)   |  # usePmecc
39	    (sectors_code << 1)   |  # nbSectorPerPage  (bits 1-3)
40	    (oob          << 4)   |  # spareSize        (bits 4-12)
41	    (ecc_code     << 13)  |  # eccBitReq        (bits 13-15)
42	    (sector_code  << 16)  |  # sectorSize       (bits 16-17)
43	    (ecc_offset   << 18)  |  # eccOffset        (bits 18-26)
44	    (0xc          << 28)     # key = valid      (bits 28-31)
45	)
46	
47	hdr = struct.pack("<I", word) * 52   # 208 bytes (0xd0); code follows at 0xd0
48	data = open(inp, "rb").read()
49	open(out, "wb").write(hdr + data)
50	print("PMECC header word 0x%08x (page=%d oob=%d ecc=%d sector=%d, eccOffset=%d); "
51	      "code at 0x%x; wrote %s (%d bytes)"
52	      % (word, page, oob, ecc, sector, ecc_offset, len(hdr), out, len(hdr) + len(data)))
53	PY
54
```

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rebuild the four at91bootstrap binaries for marvin with the blue LED channel
# repurposed to PC18, driven low (output low) at boot. Override is applied to
# .config after `make <defconfig>` (upstream clone stays vanilla).
set -euo pipefail

export PATH="/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH"
SRC="$HOME/Projects/microchip/at91bootstrap"
DST="$HOME/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/binaries"
CC=arm-none-eabi-

cd "$SRC"

# Apply the PC18-low override to the current .config (blue channel).
apply_pc18_override() {
  sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_PIN=18|' .config
  if grep -q '^CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=' .config; then
    sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=.*|CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=0|' .config
  else
    echo 'CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE=0' >> .config
  fi
  echo ">>> override applied:"; grep -E '^CONFIG_LED_B_(ON_PIOC|PIN|VALUE)=' .config
}

echo "=================== 1/4  JTAG bkptnone ELF ==================="
make mrproper
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone_defconfig
apply_pc18_override
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC
cp build/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf "$DST/"

echo "=================== 2/4  NAND bootstrap ==================="
make mrproper
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC sam9x75_curiosity_pronf_uboot_defconfig
apply_pc18_override
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC
cp build/binaries/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin "$DST/"

echo "=================== 3/4  QSPI bootstrap ==================="
make mrproper
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC sam9x75_curiosity_prodf_qspi_uboot_defconfig
apply_pc18_override
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC
cp build/binaries/sam9x7-dataflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin "$DST/"

echo "=================== 4/4  microSD bootstrap (harmony.bin) ==================="
make mrproper
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC sam9x75_curiosity_prosd_uboot_defconfig
sed -i '' 's|^CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME=.*|CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME="harmony.bin"|' .config
apply_pc18_override
make CROSS_COMPILE=$CC
cp build/binaries/sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin "$DST/"

echo "=================== PMECC header for NAND ==================="
"$DST/make-pmecchead.sh"

echo "=================== DONE ==================="
ls -la "$DST"/*.elf "$DST"/*.bin

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:17:35Z)**_

Found the bug. `make` does **not** regenerate `autoconf.h` from a hand-edited `.config` — `autoconf.h` is frozen at the `defconfig` step. (The SD `IMAGE_NAME` override works only because the *Makefile* reads `CONFIG_IMAGE_NAME` from `.config` directly as a `-D` flag; `CONFIG_LED_B_PIN` instead flows through the C `autoconf.h`.) I need to re-run kconfig after the sed. Let me confirm `olddefconfig` fixes it:

Done. All four at91bootstrap binaries are rebuilt with the blue LED channel repurposed to **PC18, output low**.

## What changed

**The override** (build-time, via `.config` — upstream clone stays vanilla):
- `CONFIG_LED_B_PIN` 20 → **18**
- `CONFIG_LED_B_VALUE` = **0** (output low)
- R (PC14) and G (PC21) untouched

This rides at91bootstrap's existing one-shot `at91_leds_init()` → `pio_set_gpio_output(PC18, 0)` = output enable, pull-up off, drive low. No source edits.

**Rebuilt & copied to [binaries/](firmware/marvin/binaries/):**
- `sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf` (JTAG load-to-RAM)
- `sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin` + `-pmecchead.bin`
- `sam9x7-dataflashboot-uboot-4.0.13.bin` (QSPI)
- `sam9x7-sdcardboot-harmony-4.0.13.bin` (SD)

(The u-boot NAND flasher has no LEDs — not rebuilt.)

## The one gotcha worth flagging

A plain `make` does **not** regenerate the C header (`autoconf.h`) after a hand-edit of `.config` — my first pass silently kept PC20. `CONFIG_LED_B_PIN` flows through `autoconf.h`, so the edit needs `make oldconfig` after the sed to take. (This differs from the SD `IMAGE_NAME` override, which the Makefile reads straight from `.config` as a `-D` flag, so it never needed `oldconfig`.) Verified in the ELF disassembly: blue is now `pio_set_gpio_output(82, 0)` — `0x52` = PIOC·32+18, low.

**Documented in:**
- [binaries/README.md](firmware/marvin/binaries/README.md) — new "Marvin customization" section + the override (with the `oldconfig` note) wired into all four recipes.
- [marvin journal](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) session log.

Nothing committed — let me know if you'd like me to stage these (the 5 rebuilt binaries + README + journal).
